title: SpaceX's first earnings reveal the cost of becoming an AI giant: Chart of the Day
excerpt: SpaceX is becoming an AI giant faster than expected — and it's spending like one.
content_html:
SpaceX (SPCX) is becoming an AI giant faster than expected — it is also spending like one.

The company's first quarterly report as a public company showed its AI business growing rapidly and swinging to an adjusted profit. But SpaceX spent nearly $16 billion on AI infrastructure during the quarter — more than six times the segment's revenue.

Space stock fell 10% in early trading Wednesday and was on track for its second-worst daily return since its June IPO.

That advances a shift visible before the IPO. SpaceX entered the public market with a rocket company reputation, but its own filings pointed investors toward AI.

AI revenue more than tripled from the first quarter to $2.6 billion. Adjusted EBITDA swung from a $609 million loss to a $1.1 billion profit.

Adjusted EBITDA strips out depreciation, stock compensation, and several other expenses. It can show whether an operation is covering its immediate costs, but it does not capture the full price of building the infrastructure behind it.

By conventional accounting, SpaceX's AI segment still lost $1.3 billion from operations.

Then came the much larger number.

Capital spending on AI jumped to $15.8 billion from $7.7 billion in the first quarter and just $749 million a year earlier. AI accounted for more than 86% of SpaceX's total capital spending during the quarter.

The spending went toward expanding SpaceX's computing capacity, including the continued build-out of its Colossus II data center. The company ended June with 1.4 gigawatts of capacity, up from 1 gigawatt three months earlier.

New customers are beginning to fill that capacity.

SpaceX signed several cloud services agreements representing $14.1 billion in contracted sales. Those deals produced $1.6 billion in incremental AI infrastructure revenue during the quarter.

That helped push companywide revenue to $7.8 billion, up 92% from a year ago and well above Wall Street estimates. Adjusted EBITDA reached $3.5 billion, nearly triple the prior-year level.

The cash picture remains far less forgiving.

During the first six months of the year, SpaceX generated $3.5 billion in cash from its operations. It spent $28.5 billion on capital projects, including $23.6 billion on AI.

SpaceX has the money to keep going. Its blockbuster initial public offering raised nearly $86 billion, and the company ended June with about $100 billion in cash, equivalents, and marketable securities.

SpaceX shares rallied over 9% Tuesday for their best day since the IPO, only one session after touching an all-time low near $105.

content_html_zh:
SpaceX (SPCX) 正在以比预期更快的速度成为一家人工智能巨头，而且它的支出也同样如此。

该公司作为上市公司的第一份季度报告显示，其人工智能业务快速增长，并开始实现调整后的利润。 但 SpaceX 本季度在人工智能基础设施上花费了近 160 亿美元，是该部门收入的六倍多。

太空股周三早盘下跌 10%，有望创下自 6 月 IPO 以来第二差的日回报率。

这推进了首次公开募股之前可见的转变。 SpaceX 凭借火箭公司的声誉进入公开市场，但其自身的文件却将投资者引向了人工智能。

AI 收入较第一季度增长两倍多，达到 26 亿美元。 调整后 EBITDA 从 6.09 亿美元亏损转为 11 亿美元利润。

调整后的 EBITDA 扣除了折旧、股票补偿和其他几项费用。 它可以显示一项操作是否覆盖了其直接成本，但它并没有捕获其背后建设基础设施的全部成本。

按照传统会计方法，SpaceX 的人工智能业务运营仍亏损 13 亿美元。

然后是更大的数字。

人工智能的资本支出从第一季度的 77 亿美元跃升至 158 亿美元，而去年同期仅为 7.49 亿美元。 人工智能占 SpaceX 本季度总资本支出的 86% 以上。

这笔支出用于扩大 SpaceX 的计算能力，包括继续扩建其 Colossus II 数据中心。 截至 6 月，该公司产能为 1.4 吉瓦，高于三个月前的 1 吉瓦。

新客户开始填补这一容量。

SpaceX 签署了多项云服务协议，合同销售额达 141 亿美元。 这些交易在本季度增加了 16 亿美元的人工智能基础设施收入。

这使得公司整体收入达到 78 亿美元，比一年前增长 92%，远高于华尔街的预期。 调整后 EBITDA 达到 35 亿美元，几乎是上年水平的三倍。

现金状况仍然不容乐观。

今年前六个月，SpaceX 的运营产生了 35 亿美元的现金。 它在资本项目上花费了 285 亿美元，其中人工智能项目花费了 236 亿美元。

SpaceX 有足够的资金继续发展。 其轰动一时的首次公开募股筹集了近 860 亿美元，截至 6 月，该公司拥有约 1000 亿美元的现金、等价物和有价证券。

周二，SpaceX 股价上涨超过 9%，创下 IPO 以来最好单日涨幅，仅一个交易日就触及 105 美元附近的历史低点。
